items.title: Tom Varner interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, August 13, 2025
items.q: I used to talk about that with the arranger/composer Jim McNeely, that he would say, “The horn is kind of like this glue.

ctx.x: were playing the trumpet. We’re so used to that trumpet-sax – you know, all through bebop – and the tone quality of the horn just makes it like a new thing.

Yeah. Yeah. It’s true. I used to talk about that with the arranger/composer Jim McNeely, that he would say, “The horn is kind of like this glue. If it’s a larger ensemble and there’s a horn inside there you might not hear, like, ‘Oh there’s a French horn in there.’ But if you take away the horn you’re going, ‘Oh that’s totally different.’” It provides this – well he used the word “glue” between the different instruments. And it’s true. The overtones of the sax and the overtones of the French horn are such that…

Some of those tougher lines that you’ve written I almost wondered like you were writing them knowing that a really good sax player could play them, and then you almost forgot that you had to play it too.
